question.problem: Consider the collection of point masses ${m}_{1}=3\,\text{kg},$ ${m}_{2}=5\,\text{kg},$ and ${m}_{3}=6\,\text{kg}$ located at ${x}_{1}=2,$ ${x}_{2}=4,$ and ${x}_{3}=5,$ respectively, along the $x$-axis, where the $x$-coordinates are measured in meters. What is the $x$-coordinate of the center of mass for this system?
question.worked_solution:
The center of mass, denoted $\overset{―}{x},$ of a collection of point masses ${m}_{1},{m}_{2},…,{m}_{n}$ located at ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ along the $x$-axis is given by 

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{O}}{m},
$$

 

where 

- $m={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{m}_{i}$ is the total mass of the system,

- ${M}_{O}={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{m}_{i}{x}_{i}$ is the total moment of the system about the origin $O.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{1} & =3, & \,{m}_{2} & =5, & \,{m}_{3} & =6, \\ {x}_{1} & =2, & \,{x}_{2} & =4, & \,{x}_{3} & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the total mass of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{m}_{i} \\  & ={m}_{1}+{m}_{2}+{m}_{3} \\  & =3+5+6 \\  & =14\,\text{kg}\end{aligned}
$$

and the moment of the system about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{m}_{i}{x}_{i} \\  & ={m}_{1}{x}_{1}+{m}_{2}{x}_{2}+{m}_{3}{x}_{3} \\  & =3\cdot 2+5\cdot 4+6\cdot 5 \\  & =6+20+30 \\  & =56\,\text{kg}\cdot \text{m}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{O}}{m}=\frac{56}{14}=4.
$$
